target.definition: Number of registered unemployed persons in Germany in October 2026, not seasonally adjusted, as first reported in the Bundesagentur für Arbeit monthly labour market press release.

inputs.name: unemployed_prior_october
inputs.description: Registered unemployed in Germany in October 2025 (not seasonally adjusted), the most recent October figure known before the estimate date

provenance.rationale: Recent October non-seasonally-adjusted levels have hovered around 2.7-2.9 million as unemployment drifted up from 2023 to 2025

inputs.name: annual_change_factor
inputs.description: Year-over-year multiplicative change in October unemployment from 2025 to 2026

provenance.rationale: Weak German labour market with modest further increase, but uncertainty in either direction

inputs.name: labour_force
inputs.description: German labour force (employed plus unemployed, ILO/domestic concept)

provenance.rationale: German labour force is roughly 46-47 million
October rates have been around 5.7-6.2% in recent years, trending slightly up

inputs.name: registered_share_of_ilo_unemployed
inputs.description: Ratio of registered unemployed (BA count) to ILO/domestic-concept unemployed persons

provenance.rationale: Registered counts and survey-based unemployment are close in Germany, with registered slightly higher in recent years

inputs.name: employed_persons
inputs.description: Number of employed persons in Germany (domestic concept)

provenance.rationale: German employment has been near 45.5-46 million

inputs.name: unemployed_per_employed
inputs.description: Ratio of registered unemployed to employed persons in October

provenance.rationale: Implied by roughly 2.8 million unemployed against roughly 45.6 million employed

inputs.name: vacancies
inputs.description: Registered job vacancies in Germany in October 2026

provenance.rationale: Registered vacancies have fallen from over 800k in 2022 toward 600-700k

inputs.name: unemployed_per_vacancy
inputs.description: Ratio of registered unemployed to registered vacancies (a labour-market tightness proxy)

provenance.rationale: Beveridge-curve ratio has risen as matching efficiency fell, roughly 4-5 unemployed per vacancy

paths.description: Scale last October's non-seasonally-adjusted registered count by the year-over-year change
Labour force times October unemployment rate, adjusted for registered-vs-survey coverage
Employed persons times unemployed-per-employed ratio; cross-check via vacancies times unemployed-per-vacancy
